fresh_provider_competent_baseline.contrastive_result: FALSUM agrees 66/66 with the separately implemented exact-target interval baseline; this validates reproducibility, not superiority.

missing_evidence_contrast.contrastive_result: FALSUM rejects 3/3 clean-looking answers that explicitly lack reviewable code/configuration evidence; verdict-only accepts 3/3 and count-plus-verdict accepts 2/3.

published_external_policy_population.contrastive_result: FALSUM removes 8 vulnerable-label PASS outcomes versus count-only, but ties verdict-only and flags 5/22 audited controls; no superiority claim is made.

version_boundary_contrast.contrastive_result: FALSUM suppresses both independently reviewed version-inapplicable references while the recorded accept-all policy displays both.

limits: The cross-source report is a new analysis of authenticated prior studies, not a claim that every underlying case is an unseen blind holdout.
External maintainer corroboration and GitHub-reviewed advisory records are defensible checks, not qualified human AppSec gold.
Published application labels are external records; audited controls are not proven bug-free and archived settlement metadata is not live settlement proof.
The fresh-provider comparison has no FALSUM-versus-baseline delta and therefore proves no ranking superiority.
No independent customer adoption, registered network evaluator, maintainer acceptance, or H2 submission is claimed.

measurement_conclusion.summary: FALSUM demonstrates two source-bound, safety-relevant contrasts against weaker policies, ties a competent version-aware baseline on fresh evidence, and preserves the negative finding that it does not beat verdict-only on the published application population.

measurement_scope.new_analysis: Predeclared cross-source comparison of evidence-sensitive policy contrasts and fair baselines; no underlying source row is relabeled.
